text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped nearly 4% today, extending a 22% gain over two weeks, as Middle East tensions escalated the price of crude oil and tightened diesel markets — exactly the conditions that boost refiner profits. Attacks on Saudi Arabia's Aramco facilities and threats from Iran triggered concerns about global oil supply disruptions, pushing world oil prices to $125 a barrel (the U.S. benchmark sits lower at $96). Refineries are already running at 92.7% capacity, and diesel inventories are unusually lean at 105 million barrels; the IEA warned this squeeze will persist into 2027, meaning refiners can sell fuel at wider profit margins as they process available crude into scarce products.

This two-week rally reflects the structural advantage refiners face when geopolitical shocks create supply anxiety and inventory tightness simultaneously. The company benefits not just from higher crude prices, but from the gap between crude and refined product prices widening — diesel in particular is now a premium product with constrained supply and steady demand.
